title: Developer Fidelity Preflight Playbook
author: Anika Rao
content:
Summary

This playbook describes the Developer Fidelity Preflight feature (D-FP): an interactive, per-route preflight estimator and policy surface that predicts request-level latency, token cost, and fidelity delta for a chosen fidelity preset before the call is sent to production. The goal is to give engineers actionable, low-friction guidance during development so they can make informed fidelity/cost tradeoffs and avoid unexpected billing or regression events.

Why this matters

- Customers and developers frequently overprovision fidelity for low-risk uses, increasing cost.
- Changes to prompts, sequence lengths, or model variants produce non-linear cost and latency effects.
- Existing offline cost simulators are helpful, but they lack per-route, on-demand estimates integrated into the developer sandbox and CI preflight checks.

Goals

1. Provide sub-second preflight estimates for expected latency and token cost for a single request or small batch in the developer sandbox and via an API.
2. Surface an estimated fidelity delta (classifier-based score) vs. a baseline variant to inform quality tradeoffs.
3. Integrate with feature-flagged rollouts and CI gates so teams can require preflight checks before releasing changes.
4. Make the estimator conservative (bias toward underpromising) and auditable.

Scope

In scope:
- Developer sandbox UX (Console & CLI) showing cost/latency/fidelity preview for sample prompts.
- Preflight API (/v1/preflight) that returns numeric estimates and confidence bands.
- CI plugin that can block pipelines if preflight exceeds route-level budgets.
- Telemetry and sample prompt trace capture to calibrate models.

Out of scope for M1:
- Full simulation of heavy production microburst traffic.
- Billing enforcement (preflight is advisory; enforcement handled separately via quotas/feature flags).

Personas

- Product Engineer: Uses preflight to check new prompt versions before shipping.
- Platform/DevOps: Adds preflight checks to CI to avoid unexpected production cost spikes.
- Solutions Engineer: Demonstrates cost/fidelity tradeoffs during POC.

User journeys

1) Developer sandbox flow (Console):
   - Open route in Console -> click "Preflight Preview" -> paste prompt -> select fidelity preset -> preview shows estimated latency (p50/p95), token cost, and fidelity delta relative to baseline, with recommended preset tweaks.
2) CLI preflight:
   - run: redwood preflight --route my-app/chat --model redwood-3-medium --preset balanced --prompt-file example.txt
   - Exit code indicates pass/fail against configured route budget.
3) CI gating:
   - Add preflight plugin to pipeline; on failure, pipeline mark is failed and a ticket is created for the owning team.

API Spec (initial)

Endpoint: POST /v1/preflight\Auth: API key scope: preflight.read
Request JSON example:
{
  "route": "my-app/chat",
  "model": "gptx-redwood-3.1",
  "preset": "balanced",
  "prompts": ["Summarize the following: ..."],
  "max_tokens": 256,
  "batch_size": 1,
  "context_stats": {"avg_input_len": 120}  // optional sandbox hint
}
Response JSON example:
{
  "estimates": {
    "latency_ms": {"p50": "68", "p95": "122"},
    "token_cost_cents": {"tokens": "0.28", "confidence": "0.85"},
    "fidelity_delta": {"score": "-0.03", "metric": "rouge-l", "confidence": "0.72"}
  },
  "recommendation": "use 'economy' preset for <10% fidelity loss and 45% cost savings",
  "warnings": ["Model variant gptx-redwood-3.1 is low on regional capacity; estimate may be optimistic"],
  "estimate_id": "pf-2026-05-04-abc123"
}

Estimator design (high level)

- Runtime profiler: low-overhead offline benchmark table per model variant, sequence length bucket, and hardware class (A100, H100, T4). Contains p50/p95 per-token latencies and base token generation overheads.
- Heuristic calculator: combines profiler with prompt length, prefix caching chance, and batch size to compute latency estimate.
- Fidelity predictor: light-weight classifier/regressor (calibrated on eval sets and customer telemetry) that returns a numerical delta against a baseline variant for a small set of metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/EMBED_SIM/heuristic-safety-score).
- Conservative adjustments: safety margins applied per-route using route-configured safety_multiplier (default 1.15 for latency, 1.25 for cost).

Configuration table (route defaults)

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| route_preflight_enabled | boolean | true | Whether preflight is accessible from Console/API for the route |
| safety_multiplier_latency | float | 1.15 | Multiply p95 latency by this factor for CI gates |
| safety_multiplier_cost | float | 1.25 | Multiply estimated cost by this factor for budget checks |
| baseline_variant | string | gptx-redwood-3-base | Variant used for fidelity delta comparisons |
| allowed_preset_list | list | [balanced, economy, fidelity] | Presets presented in Console for the route |
| preflight_block_thresholds | json-string | {"cost_cents": 100, "p95_latency_ms": 500, "fidelity_delta_worse_than": 0.05} | Route-level thresholds that can block pipelines (stored as JSON string) |

Acceptance criteria (M1)

- Console preflight UI returns results within 1s for common developer flows (average prompt <= 300 tokens).
- API preflight p95 latency < 300ms for end-to-end request (estimation only).
- CI plugin integrates with GitHub Actions and supports blocking based on route_preflight thresholds.
- Initial calibration against telemetry achieves mean absolute error (MAE) <= 12% for cost and <= 18% for latency on held-out test set.

Telemetry and calibration

- Collector: Optional sample of real requests (consent-based) will be captured from sandbox and opt-in production routes with masked PII. Stored snippets and actual token counts feed retraining.
- Metrics emitted: preflight.estimate_id, preflight.latency_est_ms.{p50,p95}, preflight.estimated_cost_cents, preflight.fidelity_delta_score, preflight.confidence.
- Calibration cadence: weekly automated re-fit job using the latest 7 days of telemetry with manual review for large drifts (>10% median error).

Security and privacy

- Developer prompts sent to preflight will be processed in the same tenancy and with the same region choices as the route; enterprise customers can opt-out of sample collection.
- For private deployments, preflight runs inside the customer's VPC using the private preflight agent.

Rollout plan

1) Alpha (internal teams only, 2026-06): Console & API with a small set of models and presets.
2) Beta (selected customers, 2026-08): Add CI plugin, route-level thresholds, and enterprise opt-in sample capture.
3) GA (2026-11): Broad availability, docs, SDK support (Python/JS), and GA API spec.

Monitoring and SLOs

- Preflight API availability: 99.9% (target).
- Console preflight perceived latency (UI quick result): p95 < 1s.
- Estimation accuracy: MAE for cost <= 12% and for latency <= 18% (monitor weekly).

Ownership and stakeholders

- Product owner: Anika Rao (Product).
- Engineering lead: Marcus Chen (eng-platform).
- Applied ML lead: Priya Patel (applied-ml-and-evals).
- Security contact: Diego Alvarez (security-and-compliance).

Operational runbook (basic)

1. Symptoms: Console preflight errors or wild estimate drift noted on dashboards.
2. Check service health: logs in /services/preflight, CPU/GPU usage, and profiler table freshness.
3. Quick mitigation: apply tighter safety_multiplier in route config or disable route_preflight_enabled for the route.
4. Postmortem: if estimation drift >25% across a week, open a cross-team incident and revert the latest calibrations.

Open questions and next steps

- Which fidelity metrics should be first-class (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity/safety heuristics)? Proposal: start with embed-sim and rouge-l plus a simple safety flag.
- How to price a potential enterprise add-on (preflight SLA and private VPC preflight agent)? Finance & Pricing to propose packaging.
- Experimentation: run A/B with conservative vs. aggressive safety_multipliers to measure developer behavior.

Appendix: Example CLI commands and CI hook

CLI:
redwood preflight --route my-app/chat --model gptx-redwood-3.1 --preset balanced --prompt-file example.txt

GitHub Actions snippet:
- name: Redwood Preflight
  uses: redwoodinc/preflight-action@v1
  with:
    api_key: ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY }}
    route: my-app/chat
    model: gptx-redwood-3.1
    preset: balanced
    fail_on: '{"p95_latency_ms": 500, "cost_cents": 100}'

References

- Related: /confluence/product-docs/product-overview/onboarding-and-cost-advisor-playbook-2026-07-28
- Related design: /confluence/product-docs/design-specs/prescriptive-fidelity-advisor-design-2026-08-24

Notes

This playbook aims to balance developer velocity and predictable economics. Preflight is intentionally advisory for M1; enforcement and billing integration are possible follow-ups once estimation fidelity is proven.
